attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stated in his voice.

semantics.note: Firm categorical negative about future products. 'Meaningful' reflects the context, where the products are the ones meant to justify the spending. No hedge and no deadline.

contract.note: The speaker named no measure. Reading it as publicly available new applications with sustained substantial adoption and documented practical value is an ordinary reading. The contract flags the stricter 'revolutionary/economy-wide' reading. It allows vendor-hosted customer evidence if labelled.

evidence.note: Dated company disclosure. Claude Code went GA in May 2025, after the post; run-rate revenue was over $2.5B and weekly users doubled by Feb 2026. This shows sustained paid adoption, though it is not independently audited.
Vendor-hosted Rakuten account, identified as such. It reports sustained production use and practical outcomes. The speed figure covers the broader agent deployment, not Claude Code alone.
Independent RCT on early-2025 tools found a slowdown. The page itself marks the results out of date. It does not test the later adoption or value of the product in e1/e2.

reviews.rationale: Under the contract's early-resolution rule, a post-publication product (Claude Code, GA May 2025) shows sustained, substantial paid adoption by Feb 2026 (e1), plus documented practical use (e2, vendor-hosted and labelled). This contradicts the categorical 'products aren't coming.' The METR study covers earlier tools and is self-described as outdated, so it does not overturn this. One caveat: the evidence is from the vendor, not independent.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his post.

semantics.note: A sweeping historical claim, 'none ever had a plan', that the following sentence glosses as just throwing GPUs at the problem. The normalisation keeps the universal quantifier and the scale-only gloss.

contract.note: Reading 'plan' as a concrete product or deployment strategy beyond hardware, judged regardless of quality, is an ordinary reading of a universal 'none ever.' The speaker may have meant a credible path to profit. The contract flags that, and the claim is partly hyperbolic.

evidence.note: Microsoft's March 2023 announcement sets out specific generative AI functions inside Word, Excel and other apps. That is a concrete product plan before the post. Here the company's own disclosure is the plan document itself.
AWS made Bedrock generally available in Sept 2023, a deployed service for building generative AI apps. This is concrete deployment beyond buying GPUs, before the post.

reviews.rationale: The claim says none of these companies ever had a plan beyond scaling hardware. At least two companies in scope documented concrete generative AI product and deployment strategies before Dec 3, 2024: Microsoft 365 Copilot (e1) and Amazon Bedrock (e2). Whether those plans were wise or profitable is outside the contract.

attribution.note: Zitron's own forecast in his post.

semantics.note: Firm 'will' with 'at some point' and no deadline. The Orion clause is split out, apparently into a sibling claim. This proposition keeps the hyperscaler blink and the end of the AI era.

contract.note: Reading 'blink' as a major hyperscaler retreat and 'era over' as a broad, sustained end to the AI investment boom is ordinary. The contract correctly says continued investment cannot disprove an eventual forecast with no deadline.

evidence.note: Reuters report from Mar 2025 of Microsoft lease withdrawals, with other hyperscalers backfilling and Microsoft's $80B plan on track. A local pullback, not the predicted sequence.
Microsoft guided in Jul 2026 that FY27 capex will grow. This is guidance, so it neither fulfils nor disproves an eventual end.
Near-cutoff reporting (Oct 26, 2026) describes continued hyperscaler growth and capacity demand, alongside investor bubble concerns.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was given. The evidence shows a local pullback followed by continued hyperscaler expansion, so the forecast is not fulfilled by the cutoff. An open-ended 'at some point' forecast cannot be contradicted by continued expansion alone, and the early-resolution rule is not met.

attribution.note: Zitron's own forecast in his post.

semantics.note: The antecedent 'once the AI bubble pops' is preserved, as are the claimed mechanism (no other hyper-growth markets) and the predicted big-tech stock bloodbath. Firm 'will'.

contract.note: It is reasonable to treat the antecedent as a broad AI-boom collapse centred on US big tech, and 'bloodbath' as a severe, broad decline. Requiring the causal mechanism follows the speaker's 'in turn lead to'.

evidence.note: Amazon said in Apr 2026 it plans about $200B of capex in 2026, backed by customer commitments. This weighs against the antecedent having occurred.
Reuters, Oct 26–27, 2026: a sharp crash in Chinese AI stocks, set against only about a 6% Nasdaq drawdown. A regional event, so it does not establish the broad US-centred antecedent.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast with no deadline, and the antecedent (a broad AI bubble popping) is not established by the cutoff. US big-tech investment continues, and the Chinese correction is regional. Because the antecedent is unknown or unmet, the forecast is not scored.
